description: One checked inventory that keeps independent product claims, example proof levels, feedback rings, and a representative test-first workflow separate.

portfolioGuidance.interpretation: Review each product surface separately. These are planning ranges, not quotas, and static policy checks are outside the denominator.
portfolioGuidance.note: The repository has strong focused and vertical owners, but it does not yet publish a complete unique-owner count per surface. haxe.rust-oo3.101 tracks report-only measurement and affected-test observation.

conclusionAudit.currentEvidence: Beads acceptance criteria and .audit decision trails capture real recent scenarios; the required scenario fields are now documented for future behavior work.

conclusionAudit.conclusion: red test at the lowest faithful layer
conclusionAudit.currentEvidence: AGENTS.md requires contract-first testing, and the representative workflow below records the actual pre-fix failure command and reason.
Portable semantic comparisons use Haxe --interp, important generated shapes use reviewed contracts, and snapshots require review. Older fixtures do not all carry an explicit expected-result note.

conclusionAudit.conclusion: one vertical tracer bullet before permutations
conclusionAudit.currentEvidence: The immutable rust.Ref<T> to Dynamic route is checked from typed Haxe analysis through generated Rust, Cargo, and runtime output before its negative permutation matrix.
Representation, runtime, source-map, semantic-diff, package, example, Windows, and consumer lanes combine focused owners with real Cargo or system observers.
The scorecards below separate claims, but complete unique-owner ratios and failure-yield measurements remain report-only follow-up work.

conclusionAudit.conclusion: examples execute at the level they advertise
conclusionAudit.currentEvidence: Every tracked example is classified below; CI compiles authored Haxe and runs Cargo tests and the generated program for the claim-bearing matrix.

conclusionAudit.conclusion: R0-R5 feedback rings with safe affected selection
conclusionAudit.currentEvidence: Focused, hook, PR, extended, weekly, and release paths exist. Semantic-owner affected selection is not yet allowed to remove PR checks; haxe.rust-oo3.101 owns observation mode first.
thinking:xhigh work requires a second pass, normally an exact-commit Oracle review, and the checklist below challenges test sensitivity and claim boundaries.

surfaces.name: Portable regular-Haxe compiler behavior
protectedClaims: Supported regular Haxe programs preserve the reviewed Haxe behavior when compiled to Rust.
Portable standard-library inventory coverage is not presented as blanket runtime parity.

verticalOwners.observer: Haxe --interp compared with generated Rust run
generated Cargo check across the Tier1 portable module inventory

residualRisks: A pinned official Haxe target-qualification checkout is not yet integrated; haxe.rust-oo3.102 owns that bounded smoke.

surfaces.name: Representation, lowering, ownership, borrowing, traits, and metal
protectedClaims: Typed representation and borrow decisions agree with emitted Rust ownership behavior.
Rust-native metal routes remain separate from portable Haxe compatibility claims.

verticalOwners.observer: saved decision audit, generated Rust shape, Cargo check, and runtime stdout
generated Rust, rustfmt, Cargo build, and reviewed output

residualRisks: The broad architecture-capability epic remains open; this scorecard covers only named admitted routes.

surfaces.name: Runtime-backed Haxe behavior
protectedClaims: Runtime helpers are used only where runtime state or Haxe behavior requires them.
Identity, lifecycle, exception, reflection, thread, and platform behavior is proved at a real runtime boundary.

verticalOwners.observer: Haxe and generated Rust runtime comparison

residualRisks: Green runtime checks do not advance no-hxrt claims.

surfaces.name: No-hxrt eligibility and emitted dependency absence
protectedClaims: Eligible programs emit and build without hxrt.
Ineligible source fails at the exact Haxe boundary before a late generated-Rust backstop becomes the normal detector.

verticalOwners.observer: cold generated crate inspection and Cargo build

residualRisks: Warm compiler state is never accepted as release proof for dependency absence; exact-profile cold generation remains required.

surfaces.name: Diagnostics and deterministic source mapping
protectedClaims: Errors point to the exact stable Haxe location without leaking machine paths.
Source maps and reports are deterministic in UTF-8 byte coordinates.

verticalOwners.observer: real compiler diagnostics from authored Haxe
generated Rust map plus exact original content

residualRisks: Broader transformed-origin coverage remains tracked separately from the exact boundaries already admitted.

surfaces.name: Cargo, package, downstream, release, and platform behavior
protectedClaims: Generated Cargo projects build with the supported Rust policy and reviewed dependency graph.
The release package is rebuilt from reviewed inputs and verified independently of the candidate archive.
Downstream and platform checks stay separate from compiler semantic claims.

verticalOwners.observer: clean Haxelib install, Haxe compile, Cargo build, and run
reviewed locks in clean workspaces with isolated Cargo homes on the exact minimum toolchain

residualRisks: Professional legal approval is separate from engineering release-integrity checks.

feedbackRings.name: focused owner
feedbackRings.currentCommand: npm run test:rust-representation-plan (or the named smallest owner)
feedbackRings.claim: Fast diagnosis for one behavior owner.
feedbackRings.cacheRule: Warm reuse is allowed for iteration, but not for no-hxrt or release proof.

feedbackRings.name: local smoke and pre-commit
feedbackRings.currentCommand: installed scripts/hooks/pre-commit plus npm run hooks:check
feedbackRings.claim: Changed high-risk contracts and deterministic generated records are checked before commit.
feedbackRings.selection: path triggers with fail-closed freshness checks
feedbackRings.cacheRule: Developer caches are allowed; generated evidence must remain byte-identical.

feedbackRings.name: required pull request
feedbackRings.claim: All required product surfaces run independently on every pull request.
feedbackRings.selection: broad required shards; no semantic test is removed by an affected selector
feedbackRings.cacheRule: Tool downloads may be cached; product outputs are regenerated.

feedbackRings.name: extended
feedbackRings.currentCommand: npm run test:upstream-stdlib:tier2 plus PR performance and platform jobs
feedbackRings.claim: Broader inventory, performance, and platform pressure tests the required path.
feedbackRings.selection: currently broad rather than affected; observation-mode semantic selection is deferred to haxe.rust-oo3.101
feedbackRings.cacheRule: Selector misses cannot hide because the broad job remains active.

feedbackRings.name: full and weekly
feedbackRings.claim: Full Linux, Windows, downstream, and evidence paths catch cross-surface interactions.
feedbackRings.cacheRule: Caches may speed tools; immutable reports and clean generated outputs remain separate.

feedbackRings.name: release
feedbackRings.currentCommand: .github/workflows/ci.yml release job and npm run test:release
feedbackRings.claim: The exact tested commit is rebuilt and its package is verified from reviewed inputs.
feedbackRings.selection: release policy only; never affected-path selection
feedbackRings.cacheRule: Cold exact-profile proof is required; a warm compiler cache cannot prove no-hxrt or release behavior.

retryPolicy.networkBootstrapRetries: allowed only around external downloads and must not hide a product-test failure
retryPolicy.quarantine: A claim-bearing test may be quarantined only with an owner, expiry, Bead, preserved failure artifact, and another active proof for the same public claim.

highRiskReviewChecklist: Did the new or changed test fail for the intended reason before the fix?
Is the expected result independent of the implementation being tested?
Are important negative and edge cases missing?
Does a mock remove the boundary named by the claim?
Could path-based selection skip the real semantic owner?
Is a green result from one product surface being used to advance another surface?
Does the public wording claim more than the observed compile, build, runtime, package, or platform level?

representativeWorkflow.title: Scoped Rust borrow hidden inside a runtime anonymous record

scenario.preconditions: A typed anonymous record declares an optional field whose transparent Haxe type ultimately contains a scoped Rust borrow.
scenario.action: Compile a runtime-name reflection write and typed read through the representation-plan fixture.
scenario.observableResult: Compilation reports HXRS-BORROW-REGION at the Haxe value before any Rust source directory is created.
scenario.edgeBehavior: Deep acyclic wrappers and abstracts around the whole record are rejected, while equally deep owned values and recursive owned records remain accepted.
scenario.protectedClaim: Runtime anonymous records cannot store an owned value under a field later exposed as a scoped Rust borrow.

redState.failure: The deep wrapper, outer-record abstract, and omitted mutable-borrow field compiled past the intended early check.

expectedResult.source: Haxe transparent-type meaning plus the reviewed Rust Anon::get<T> owned-value and lifetime contract
expectedResult.independence: The expectation comes from the source-language type and Rust lifetime rules, not from reusing the emitter's classification algorithm.

tracerBullet.result: The saved decision is consumed once, generated Rust copies or clones the owned referent, Cargo accepts it, and runtime prints 7|hello|true without a borrow escaping.

broaderProof.result: Passed in 7201 seconds across 138 snapshots, 36 portable behavior comparisons, runtime, package, examples, and policy gates.
